But the fillable contract is declared with App\Models\Queue.php:11 / App\Models/Ticket.php:16-25 using `Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Attributes\Fillable`, a class absent from Laravel 12.x (verified against framework v12.62.0, whose getFillable() only returns $this->fillable), so on a 12.x project the core `Ticket::create()`/`update()` writes fail; see issue 1.

scope.evidence: Everything in the diff serves the task: the two migrations, Queue/Ticket models, enums, exception, action, factories, one test file, plus the docs and CHANGELOG updates the task/conventions require. The only schema addition, queues.last_ticket_number (...create_queues_table.php:24), is needed to honour 'deleting a ticket does not reuse its number'.

issues.explanation: Fillable fields are declared with `#[Fillable([...])]` from `Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Attributes\Fillable`, a class that does not exist in Laravel 12.x (the framework available here, v12.62.0, has no such attribute and getFillable() returns only $this->fillable); on a 12.x project this silently leaves $fillable empty, so `Ticket::create()` in IssueTicket and `$ticket->update()` in call() throw MassAssignmentException — use `protected $fillable = [...]` or confirm the pinned version actually supports the attribute.

The create() override only serializes count() creation when no attributes are passed, so `Ticket::factory()->forQueue($queue)->count(2)->create(['priority' => 5])` allocates A001 twice and hits the (queue_id, code) unique index; the workaround should also cover the attributes path (or allocate codes at store time).

The retry-on-unique-collision behaviour, which the task explicitly requires, has no test; a test that forces a QueryException on the first attempt would lock in the MAX_ATTEMPTS/unique-violation logic.

Using `max($highWater, $lastValid)` makes code allocation diverge from 'last valid code + 1 by insertion order' for out-of-order valid legacy codes: with A999 inserted and then A001, the spec's insertion-order rule gives A002 while this returns A1000.

Call authorization is an inline EntityMembership existence query; conventions require authorization to go through policies/gates (app/Policies), so a TicketPolicy ability (or a gate) should own this check.
The deleting-time high-water bump is redundant for Eloquent-created tickets (created already advanced it), and nextCode plucks every code for the queue, which grows unbounded per issuance.
The new CHANGELOG bullet drops the PR-link style used by every neighbouring entry, and database-schema.md still ends without a trailing newline.

review.summary: The change implements the queue/ticket core thoroughly: migrations, models with enums/casts/factories, per-queue display codes, the IssueTicket action with a locked queue re-check and collision retries, write-once and single-call guards, plus a broad Pest suite and the required docs/CHANGELOG updates. It is close to approvable, but the models declare mass assignment via `Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Attributes\Fillable`, which does not exist in Laravel 12.x and would leave $fillable empty so the core issuance/call writes throw, and the custom factory create() still duplicates codes for count() with attributes. Remaining concerns are smaller: no retry/collision test, high-water vs insertion-order semantics, and inline authorization instead of a policy.
